# NSPanel HAUI 0.5.8

0.5.8 is about ownership and reach. The hub's own settings are editable in Home Assistant now — its name, and the three time and date formats every panel inherits — and every grip in the editor drags with a finger, so reordering a Fleet card, a panel, an item or a swipe no longer needs a mouse. **Repair display** arrives for a display that cannot take its 11 MB file. In the editor, every text now takes its role's size instead of drifting, the screens centre a column instead of stretching across a wide monitor, and on Fleet the two overview cards close on footers, over a quieter band.

This release changes the integration, the editor and the display file's version: the two TFTs now report **1.1.0**, so a repair leaves the same number an ordinary install does, and a panel installs the file once through the normal display update. The pages themselves are unchanged — only `system.tftVersion` moved.

## Hub settings in Home Assistant

Until now the hub was named when it was created and every other setting belonged to a panel, so the formats a panel fell back to were only reachable through the panel itself. **Settings → Devices & services → NSPanel HAUI → Configure** now opens a form for the hub's own settings.

**Hub name** is the name Home Assistant shows for this integration: on its card, in the repair that warns about a hub without enabled devices, and in the log lines about the hub. It renames nothing else — panels keep their own names, device and entity ids keep the name they were created with, and the notify and update entities keep working across a rename.

The three formats below are what a panel inherits while its own **Time format**, **Date format** or **Locale-aware date layout** is left at **Default** in the editor:

| Setting | Example | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Default time format** | `%H:%M` | A strftime pattern; `%H:%M` is 14:30, `%I:%M %p` is 2:30 PM |
| **Default date format** | `%A, %d. %B %Y` | A strftime pattern with at least one `%` directive |
| **Default locale-aware date layout** | `full` | Used while a panel's date format is **Default**; the layout follows the panel's language |

The rules are short. A panel's own value wins, so a panel with a format of its own is untouched by these. Clearing a field means the built-in default rather than a blank panel, and the form opens on what panels inherit today. A format needs at least one `%` directive and stays at 64 characters or fewer, and a blank **Hub name** is refused — the field keeps what was typed so it can be corrected.

Saving writes the name and the options together and reloads the integration once, so every panel restarts with the new defaults: its display keeps showing the last page and is redrawn after a few seconds. Nothing is lost and the editor needs no reload ([Hub settings](docs/user/hub-settings.md)).

## Reordering with a finger

A grip was a mouse-only control. Mobile Safari and Chrome report no `dragstart` for a finger, so the reorder code — which listens for the plain HTML5 drag events — never ran, and a panel on a tablet or a phone could not be reordered at all.

A press on a grip now runs that sequence itself: `dragstart` on the element that is draggable, `dragover` on whatever sits under the finger, and `drop` plus `dragend` when it lifts. Everything downstream is unchanged, which is the point — the same drop markers, panels still cross between Navigation and Hidden in one drop, and no second drag implementation sits beside the first.

The details that make a finger usable: 6 px of travel before a press becomes a drag, so a tap stays a tap; the click a touch drag ends with is swallowed for half a second, so it no longer selects the row it landed on; one finger drags at a time, so a second one cannot mix two drags up; and a grip held within 48 px of a list's edge scrolls it up to 14 px a frame, so a card can be dragged past the fold of a long inventory ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).

## Repair display

An ordinary display update pushes 11.5 MB (landscape) or 11.3 MB (portrait) to the display. A display that is half-written, that runs at another baud, or that reboots on the way through that file never finishes the transfer, and every retry fails the same way. A repair page installs where that file cannot: about 465 KB, a twenty-fifth of the release file, because it is one page with two subset fonts rather than the pictures, the thirteen pages of widgets and the event scripts.

**Repair display** sits under the installed versions in the Device screen's **Updates** sidebar. It asks first, then installs two files: the release's repair screen for the panel's display model, and — once the panel is back from the repair's reboot, 15 seconds later — the TFT this firmware needs, through the ordinary install path, so the display update reports it as usual.

It is never automatic. A repair that fails ends the attempt, the error reaches the editor and the update entity, and nothing runs afterwards. It is offered on the same terms as an install — updates enabled, the panel connected, no install already running — and only for a display model the loaded release has a repair file for ([Repair display](docs/user/editor/device.md#repair-display), [Display repair](docs/develop/update-process.md#display-repair)).

The action, its endpoint, the manifest's `repair` block, the release workflow that publishes the assets, the check that proves a repair file and both files themselves all ship here: `nextion/nspanel_haui_repair.tft` for the landscape (`eu`) display model and `nextion/nspanel_haui_repair_portrait.tft` for the portrait (`us`) one, each compiled from a committed one-page Editor project, so a released manifest carries the `repair` block the sidebar reads ([The repair TFTs](docs/develop/nextion-editor.md#the-repair-tfts)).

## A quieter band, and Fleet footers

A card's header and footer bands were the theme's heavy grey bar. They are now one `--haui-surface-band` token that mixes 6% of the theme's text colour into the card ground, so Fleet's inventory and events cards, the Device screen's workspace strip, the sidebars' title strips and the panel groups open and close a card on the same neutral note — in light and dark themes alike, and a theme change moves all of them at once ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).

Fleet's two overview cards also close with a footer now. The inventory's **Updates** and **Integration version** figures sit under the device table instead of beside its title, as one line of `label value` runs that never wraps, and the update button keeps the title's row at its end on a phone instead of dropping to a row of its own. **Latest events** keeps **Reset**, **Last 24 hours** and **Logs** under the timeline instead of on its title line, so both headers stay short and the actions stay at hand ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).

The two cards' headers also read title then value the same way. **Latest events** now carries the window it covers — **Last 24 hours**, or **Since 14:32** once **Reset** has moved it — beside its title, right after the count, where that label used to sit in the header's bottom corner; its second line is the device scope alone, exactly as the inventory heads its own card with **connected / total** and the sentence under it ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).

## One type role per text

The editor's type had drifted, because each screen chose a size where it drew a text: the same kind of fact was 10, 12 or 13px depending on the card, a value carried weight 400 in one figure and 500 or 600 in the next, and a heading's own description could read louder than the heading it described. Every text now takes the size *and* weight of its role, and nothing picks a size of its own.

The steps that moved most are the quiet ones. **A pill is one look**: a badge, a count bubble, the repeat count and the item type chip are one step — 12px at the text weight, no uppercase — whatever their class is called, and the container that holds one no longer resizes it. **A value is 13px at 500 and the text around it 13px at 400**, so weight separates the two within a size instead of a second size doing it. A name that opens a row or a card — a Fleet card's device, an inventory row, a panel row, an item row, the dashboard card's device — takes a new 14px step between a value and a card title, while the name of a choice inside a control stays on the value step. Buttons and menu items take the 13px text step instead of inheriting the body step.

**The eyebrow is one recipe**: 10px, weight 600 and `.05em` tracking, uppercase, together in the same rule — nothing else in the editor is uppercase, tracked or 600, and a translated label is never transformed by case.

The whole ladder also sits one step below Home Assistant's own type — body text 15px to HA's 16px, card titles 15px, names and values 13px — so the dense screens read a little tighter at every depth. Every step still follows Home Assistant's font size setting, because the tokens multiply by `--ha-font-size-scale`: a larger house font grows the editor with it rather than leaving the editor alone at the old size.

None of it depends on anyone remembering the ladder. `check_frontend_styles.py` refuses a raw or off-scale size, half an eyebrow, weight 600 or tracking outside it, and a pill that resizes its own text ([Visual foundations](docs/develop/frontend-visuals.md#text-sizes)).

## A column that stops on a wide monitor

The screens' content column now stops at 1440px and centres instead of stretching to the window's width. Fleet's cards and device table and the Device screen's workspace and side stack keep their proportions on a wide monitor, where a two-column layout used to spread across the whole screen and leave the eye travelling; the titlebar and the footer stay full-bleed, so the frame still meets the edges of the window ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).

## Compiling a display file, documented

Both TFTs (1.1.0) already carry the display-side script cleanup, and recompiling the committed HMIs reproduces them byte for byte, so the developer guide records it as shipped instead of pending. [Editing the HMI](docs/develop/nextion-editor.md#compiling-a-tft) now walks through turning an `.HMI` into a `.tft` in the Nextion Editor: the two steps that make a compile, the `Component overlap` warnings that are by design, and the artifact check that proves a TFT belongs to its source ([HMI event scripts](docs/develop/nextion-scripts.md#cleanup-applied)).

## Before updating

One thing to expect: the display file moves to **1.1.0**, so every panel installs it once after the firmware update — the same 11.5 MB (landscape) or 11.3 MB (portrait) transfer as any display update. Nothing in the pages changed; the version inside the TFT is what moved, so a repaired display ends on the same number as an ordinary install and the hub stops offering the file.

Nothing else: no renamed entity, no changed service, no migration.

One thing to time: saving the hub's settings reloads the integration, so every panel restarts. Do it while nobody is using one — the display keeps its last page and is redrawn after a few seconds.

## Added

- **Hub settings on the integration card** — **Configure** opens the hub's own settings: the **Hub name** Home Assistant shows, and the **Default time format**, **Default date format** and **Default locale-aware date layout** every panel inherits while its own format is **Default**. A panel's own value wins, an empty field keeps the built-in default, and saving reloads the integration once so every panel restarts with the new defaults ([Hub settings](docs/user/hub-settings.md)).
- **Repair display in the Updates sidebar** — under the installed versions, after a confirmation, the hub installs the release's minimal repair TFT for the panel's display model and then the TFT this firmware needs, so a display that stays blank, sits on **Waiting for Initialization** or never finishes the 11 MB file is recovered from the editor instead of a Nextion Editor session. The action, the manifest's `repair` block and both repair files ship together — one page per display model with two subset fonts, about 465 KB — so a released manifest carries the block and the sidebar offers the repair ([Repair display](docs/user/editor/device.md#repair-display)).

## Changed

- **The display file reports 1.1.0** — both release TFTs carry `system.tftVersion` `1.1.0` where they carried `0.4.8`, and the firmware requires that version, so every panel installs the file once through the ordinary display update. No page, widget or script changed; the version moved so a repaired display ends on the same number an ordinary install does and so the repair file (`1`) and the release file (`1.1.0`) are told apart ([Display repair](docs/develop/update-process.md#display-repair)).
- **Card bands are a neutral step** — one `--haui-surface-band` token mixes 6% of the theme's text colour into the card ground, so every card heading and footer in the editor sits on the same quiet band, in light and dark themes alike ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **Fleet's overview cards close with a footer** — the inventory's **Updates** and **Integration version** figures sit under the device table as one unwrapping line of `label value` runs, with the update button staying on the title's row on a phone, and **Latest events** keeps **Reset**, **Last 24 hours** and **Logs** under the timeline ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **Latest events carries its window beside its title** — **Last 24 hours**, or **Since 14:32** after a reset, sits after the count on the title's line instead of in the header's bottom corner, so the second line is the device scope alone and both dashboard cards read title then value ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **One type role per text** — badges, count bubbles, the repeat count and the item type chip are one quiet 12px pill look, a value is 13px at 500 with 13px at 400 around it, the name a row or card is listed by takes a new 14px step, buttons and menu items take the 13px text step, and the eyebrow is one 10px/600/`.05em` uppercase recipe. The ladder sits one step below Home Assistant's own type and follows its font size setting, and `check_frontend_styles.py` now refuses an off-scale size, half an eyebrow or a pill that resizes its own text ([Visual foundations](docs/develop/frontend-visuals.md#text-sizes)).
- **The content column stops at 1440px** — the editor's screens centre a column of that width instead of stretching across a wide monitor, while the titlebar and the footer stay full-bleed ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **The developer guide walks through a TFT compile** — turning an `.HMI` into a `.tft` is documented step by step, with the by-design `Component overlap` warnings, and the display-side script cleanup is recorded as shipped: both TFTs already carry it and recompiling the committed HMIs reproduces them byte for byte ([Editing the HMI](docs/develop/nextion-editor.md#compiling-a-tft)).

## Fixed

- **Reordering works by touch** — a finger or a pen on a grip now drags a Fleet card or row, a panel row, an item or a swipe, where mobile Safari and Chrome start no HTML5 drag and the grip did nothing at all. The same drop markers show as for a mouse, panels still cross between Navigation and Hidden in one drop, the click a drag ends with no longer selects the row it landed on, and a grip held near the edge of a long list scrolls it ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
